value.zh: 太祖道武帝 太宗明元帝
value.en: Emperor Daowu the Grand Progenitor; Emperor Mingyuan the Grand Successor.
value.literal: Grand Progenitor Emperor Daowu; Grand Successor Emperor Mingyuan.

value.zh: 太宗明元皇帝諱嗣，道武皇帝之長子也。
value.en: Emperor Mingyuan, styled the Grand Ancestor, whose name was Si, was Dao Wu's eldest son.
value.literal: The Grand Ancestor, Emperor Mingyuan, personal name Si, was the eldest son of Emperor Dao Wu.

value.zh: 母曰劉貴人，登國七年，生於雲中宮。
value.en: His mother was Honored Lady Liu; in Dengguo year seven he was born at the Cloud Palace.
value.literal: His mother was Lady Liu the Honored; in the seventh year of Dengguo he was born in the Cloud Palace.

value.zh: 道武晚有男，聞而大悅，乃大赦。
value.en: Dao Wu had long awaited a son; when he heard, he rejoiced and proclaimed a general amnesty.
value.literal: Dao Wu had a son late in life; on hearing the news he rejoiced greatly and proclaimed a general amnesty.

value.zh: 帝明睿寬毅，非禮不動。
value.en: He was clear-minded, wise, magnanimous, and firm; nothing moved him outside the rites.
value.literal: The Emperor was bright, wise, generous, and resolute; he would not act against propriety.

value.zh: 天興六年，封齊王，拜相國。
value.en: In Tianxing year six he was made Prince of Qi and Chancellor of State.
value.literal: In the sixth year of Tianxing he was enfeoffed Prince of Qi and appointed Chancellor of State.

value.zh: 初，帝母既賜死，道武召帝告曰：「昔漢武將立其子而殺其母，不令婦人與國政，汝當繼統，故吾遠同漢武。」
value.en: When his mother had been put to death, Dao Wu called him in and said: "Emperor Wu of Han killed his son's mother before setting the boy on the throne, lest a woman hold the state. You will succeed me, so I have done as Han Wu did."
value.literal: At the outset, after the Emperor's mother had been ordered to die, Dao Wu summoned the Emperor and said: "In old days Emperor Wu of Han was about to establish his son and therefore killed the mother, not allowing women a share in state affairs; you are to succeed to the throne, so I follow Han Wu in the distant past."

value.zh: 帝素純孝，哀不自勝。
value.en: The Emperor had always been devoted; grief overwhelmed him.
value.literal: The Emperor had always been pure in filial piety; grief overwhelmed him beyond bearing.

value.zh: 道武怒。
value.en: Dao Wu grew angry.
value.literal: Dao Wu was angry.

value.zh: 帝還宮，哀不自止，道武知而又召帝。
value.en: He went back to the palace still weeping; when Dao Wu heard, he summoned him again.
value.literal: The Emperor returned to the palace; grief would not cease; Dao Wu learned of it and summoned him again.

value.zh: 帝欲入，左右諫，請待和解而進，帝從之。
value.en: He started to go in; his attendants urged him to wait until tempers had cooled; he listened.
value.literal: The Emperor wished to enter; his attendants remonstrated, asking that he wait until feelings had eased before going in; the Emperor followed their advice.

value.zh: 及元紹之逆，帝還而誅之。
value.en: When Prince Shao rebelled, the Emperor came back and put him to death.
value.literal: When Prince Shao's rebellion came, the Emperor returned and had him executed.

value.zh: 韓襃 趙肅 張軌 李彥 郭彥 梁昕 皇甫璠 辛慶之 王子直 杜杲 呂思禮 徐招 檀翥 孟信 宗懍 劉璠 柳遐
value.en: Han Bao, Zhao Su, Zhang Gui, Li Yan, Guo Yan, Liang Xin, Huang Fufan, Xing Qingzhi, Wang Zizhi, Du Gao, Lu Sili, Xu Zhao, Tan Zhu, Meng Xin, Zong Lin, Liu Fan, and Liu Xia
value.literal: Han Bao, Zhao Su, Zhang Gui, Li Yan, Guo Yan, Liang Xin, Huang Fufan, Xing Qingzhi, Wang Zizhi, Du Gao, Lu Sili, Xu Zhao, Tan Zhu, Meng Xin, Zong Lin, Liu Fan, Liu Xia

value.zh: 初，陳文帝弟安成王頊為質于梁，及江陵平，頊隨例遷長安。
value.en: Earlier, Chen Emperor Wen's younger brother, Prince Xu of Ancheng, had been held as a hostage in Liang; when Jiangling fell, Xu was moved to Chang'an with the other captives.
value.literal: Earlier, Emperor Wen of Chen's younger brother, Prince An Cheng Xu, had been a hostage in Liang; when Jiangling fell, Xu was transferred to Chang'an along with the others.

value.zh: 陳人請之，周文帝許而未遣。
value.en: Chen asked for his return; Northern Zhou Emperor Wen agreed in principle but did not yet release him.
value.literal: The Chen side requested his return; Emperor Wen of Zhou agreed but did not yet send him back.

value.zh: 至是，帝欲歸之，命杲使焉。
value.en: On this occasion the emperor decided to send Xu home and dispatched Guo as envoy.
value.literal: At this time the emperor wished to return him and ordered Guo to go as envoy.

value.zh: 陳文帝大悅，即遣使報聘，並賂黔中數州地，仍請畫野分疆，永敦鄰好。
value.en: Chen Emperor Wen was delighted, promptly sent envoys in return, offered several prefectures in Qianzhong as a gift, and asked that borders be drawn so that good relations might endure.
value.literal: Emperor Wen of Chen was greatly pleased, immediately sent envoys in return, ceded several prefectures in Qianzhong as a gift, and further requested demarcation of borders to cement neighborly friendship forever.

value.zh: 以杲奉使稱旨，進授都督，行小禦伯，更往分界。
value.en: Because Guo's embassy had fully satisfied the throne, he was promoted to regional commander and acting Junior Defender Baron and sent back to settle the frontier.
value.literal: Because Guo's mission accorded with the imperial intent, he was promoted to regional commander and acting Junior Defender Baron, and sent again to demarcate the border.

value.zh: 陳於是歸魯山郡。
value.en: Chen thereupon restored Lushan Commandery.
value.literal: Chen thereupon returned Lushan Commandery.

value.zh: 帝乃拜頊柱國大將軍，詔杲送之還國。
value.en: The Zhou emperor then enfeoffed Xu as Pillar General and ordered Guo to escort him home.
value.literal: The emperor then enfeoffed Xu as Pillar General and ordered Guo to escort him back to his country.

value.zh: 陳文帝謂杲曰：「家弟今蒙禮遣，實是周朝之惠。
value.en: Chen Emperor Wen said to Guo: "My brother has now been honorably sent home—a genuine kindness from your court.
value.literal: Emperor Wen of Chen said to Guo: "My younger brother has now received the courtesy of being sent home—this is truly a kindness from the Zhou court.

value.zh: 然不還魯山，亦恐未能及此。」
value.en: Yet had Lushan not been returned, I doubt this would have been possible".
value.literal: Yet had Lushan not been returned, I fear this might not have been possible."

value.zh: 杲答曰：「安成之在關中，乃咸陽一布衣耳。
value.en: Guo replied: "When Prince Xu of Ancheng was in Guanzhong, he was no more than a commoner of Xianyang in plain cloth.
value.literal: Guo replied: "When Prince An Cheng was in the Guanzhong region, he was no more than a common cloth-clad man of Xianyang.

value.zh: 然是陳之介弟，其價豈止一城？
value.en: Yet he is Chen's own brother—is his worth no more than one walled town?
value.literal: Yet he is Chen's honored younger brother—is his worth limited to a single city?

value.zh: 本朝親睦九族，恕己及物，上遵太祖遺旨，下思繼好之義，所以發德音者，蓋為此也。
value.en: Our court cherishes kinship through the nine degrees of relation, extends forbearance from oneself to others, honors above the founding emperor's testament and below the duty of lasting friendship—that is why this gracious decree was issued.
value.literal: Our court cherishes the nine degrees of kinship, extends forbearance from oneself to others, above observes the founding emperor's testament, below honors the duty of continuing friendly relations—the reason for issuing this gracious decree is precisely this.

value.zh: 若知止侔魯山，固當不貪一鎮。
value.en: If Prince Xu were worth no more than Lushan, we would certainly not covet a single commandery.
value.literal: If Prince Xu were worth no more than Lushan, we would certainly not be greedy for one commandery.

value.zh: 況魯山梁之舊地，梁即本朝籓臣，若以始末言之，魯山自合歸國。
value.en: Moreover Lushan was former Liang territory, and Liang was itself our court's vassal; judged by the whole course of events, Lushan ought by rights to have returned to us.
value.literal: Moreover Lushan was Liang's former territory, and Liang was itself our court's vassal—in light of the whole history, Lushan ought by rights to return to our state.

value.zh: 雲以尋常之土，易已骨肉之親，使臣猶謂不可，何以聞諸朝廷！」
value.en: To propose trading ordinary soil for one's own flesh and blood—even I find that impossible; how could I report such a thing to my court"!
value.literal: To speak of trading ordinary land for one's own kin—even your envoy finds it impossible; how could I report such a thing to our court!"

value.zh: 陳文帝慚恧久之，乃曰：「前言戲之耳！」
value.en: Chen Emperor Wen was abashed for some time, then said: "What I said before was only in jest"!
value.literal: Emperor Wen of Chen was ashamed for a long while, then said: "My earlier words were spoken in jest!"

value.zh: 自是接遇有加常禮。
value.en: From then on he treated Guo with honors beyond the usual protocol.
value.literal: From then on he received Guo with honors beyond the usual protocol.

value.zh: 及還，引升殿，親降御座，執手以別。
value.en: When Guo was leaving, the emperor led him into the hall, came down from the throne in person, and clasped his hand in farewell.
value.literal: When Guo was about to return, the emperor led him up to the hall, personally descended from the imperial seat, and clasped his hand in farewell.

value.zh: 朝廷嘉之，授大都督、小載師下大夫，行小納言，復聘于陳。
value.en: The Zhou court commended him, appointing him Grand Regional Commander, junior grand master under the Master of Carriages, and acting Junior Remonstrator, and sent him on another embassy to Chen.
value.literal: The Zhou court commended him, appointing him Grand Regional Commander, junior grand master under the Master of Carriages, acting Junior Remonstrator, and sent him on another mission to Chen.

value.zh: 及華皎來附，詔令衛公直、都督元定等援之。
value.en: When Hua Jiao defected to Zhou, an edict ordered Duke Yuwen Zhi of Wei, Regional Commander Yuan Ding, and others to go to his aid.
value.literal: When Hua Jiao came over to submit, an edict ordered Duke of Wei Yuwen Zhi, regional commander Yuan Ding, and others to support him.

value.zh: 定等並沒。
value.en: Ding and his men were wiped out.
value.literal: Ding and the others were all lost.

value.zh: 自是連兵不息，東南搔動。
value.en: From then on the fighting never let up, and the southeast was in turmoil.
value.literal: From then on fighting continued without pause and the southeast was unsettled.

value.zh: 武帝授杲禦正中大夫，使陳，論保境息人之意。
value.en: Emperor Wu appointed Guo Chief Straightening Grand Master and sent him to Chen to propose securing the borders and giving the people peace.
value.literal: Emperor Wu appointed Guo Chief Straightening Grand Master and sent him to Chen to discuss the idea of securing borders and giving the people rest.

value.zh: 陳宣帝遣其黃門侍郎徐陵謂杲曰：「兩國通好，彼朝受我叛人，何也？」
value.en: Chen Emperor Xuan sent his Gentleman at the Yellow Gate, Xu Ling, to say to Guo: "Our two states are at peace—why does your court take in our deserters"?
value.literal: Emperor Xuan of Chen sent his Gentleman at the Yellow Gate Xu Ling to say to Guo: "Our two states are on friendly terms—why does your court accept our defectors?"

value.zh: 杲曰：「陳主昔在本朝，非慕義而至，主上授以柱國，位極人臣，子女玉帛，備禮將送，今主社稷，孰謂非恩？
value.en: Guo said: "Your ruler once lived at our court—not because he admired our righteousness; our sovereign made him a Pillar of State, raised him to the highest rank, and sent him home with sons, daughters, jade, and silks in full ceremony. Now he sits upon the Chen throne—who would call that anything but grace?
value.literal: Guo said: "The Chen ruler once dwelt in our court—not because he admired our righteousness did he come; our sovereign enfeoffed him as Pillar of State, raised him to the utmost rank, and sent him off with full ceremony of sons, daughters, jade, and silks. Now he rules his realm—who would say this is not grace?

value.zh: 郝烈之徒，邊人狂狡，曾未報德，而先納之。
value.en: Men like Hao Lie were wild, cunning border folk who had never repaid a kindness, yet you took them in first.
value.literal: The likes of Hao Lie were wild and cunning border folk who had never repaid kindness, yet you took them in first.

value.zh: 今受華氏，正是相報。
value.en: Our acceptance of the Hua clan is simply repayment in kind.
value.literal: Now that we accept the Hua clan, it is precisely repayment in kind.

value.zh: 過自彼始，豈在本朝！」
value.en: The offense began on your side—how can the fault be ours"!
value.literal: The offense began on your side—how can it be laid at our court's door!"

value.zh: 陵曰：「彼納華皎，志圖吞噬。
value.en: Ling said: "In taking Hua Jiao, your court aims at swallowing us whole.
value.literal: Ling said: "In accepting Hua Jiao, your side aims at swallowing us whole.

value.zh: 此受郝烈。
value.en: In this case we took in Hao Lie.
value.literal: In this matter we accepted Hao Lie.

value.zh: 容之而已。
value.en: We merely gave him shelter—that is all.
value.literal: We merely harbored him, that is all.

value.zh: 且華皎方州列將。
value.en: Moreover Hua Jiao was a frontier commander and a ranked general.
value.literal: Moreover Hua Jiao was a regional commander and ranked general.

value.zh: 竊邑叛亡。
value.en: He seized his command and fled in rebellion.
value.literal: He seized a city and rebelled in flight.

value.zh: 郝烈一百許戶，脫身逃竄。
value.en: Hao Lie was no more than a hundred-odd households who slipped away in flight.
value.literal: Hao Lie was a mere hundred or so households who slipped away in escape.

value.zh: 大小有異，豈得同年而語乎？」
value.en: The cases differ in scale—how can they be mentioned in the same breath"?
value.literal: The scale differs—how can they be spoken of in the same breath?"

value.zh: 杲曰：「大小雖殊，受降一也。
value.en: Guo said: "Great or small, the principle of accepting surrender is the same.
value.literal: Guo said: "Though the scale differs, accepting surrender is the same principle.

value.zh: 若論先後，本朝無失。」
value.en: If we speak of who acted first, our court was not in the wrong".
value.literal: If we speak of sequence, our court was not in the wrong."

value.zh: 陵曰：「周朝送主上還國，既以為恩，衛公共元定度江，孰云非怨？
value.en: Ling said: "Your Zhou court sent our ruler home and call that kindness; Duke Yuwen Zhi of Wei and Yuan Ding crossed the Yangtze—is that not cause for grievance?
value.literal: Ling said: "Your Zhou court sent our ruler home—you call that kindness; Duke of Wei and Yuan Ding crossed the Yangtze—is that not grounds for grievance?

value.zh: 計恩與怨，亦足相埒。」
value.en: Set kindness against grievance, and the two are enough to cancel each other out".
value.literal: Counting kindness against grievance, they are sufficient to balance each other."

value.zh: 杲曰：「元定等軍敗身囚，其怨已滅。
value.en: Guo said: "Yuan Ding and his men were defeated and taken prisoner—the grievance from that is already spent.
value.literal: Guo said: "Yuan Ding and the others were defeated and taken captive—their grievance is already extinguished.

value.zh: 陳主負扆馮玉，其恩猶在。
value.en: Your ruler sits upon the throne with the jade screen before him—the grace you received still stands.
value.literal: The Chen ruler sits upon the throne with jade before him—your grace still stands.

value.zh: 且怨由彼國，恩起本朝，以怨酬恩，未之聞也。」
value.en: Moreover the grievance came from your state and the grace from ours—to answer grace with grievance is something I have never heard of".
value.literal: Moreover the grievance arose from your state and the grace from ours—to repay grace with grievance—is unheard of."

value.zh: 陵笑而不答。
value.en: Ling smiled and said nothing.
value.literal: Ling smiled and did not reply.

value.zh: 杲因陳和通之便，陵具以聞。
value.en: Seizing the opening to discuss peace, Guo pressed his case, and Ling reported the whole exchange to his sovereign.
value.literal: Guo took advantage of the opportunity to discuss peace, and Ling reported everything to his sovereign.

value.zh: 陳宣許之，遂遣使來聘。
value.en: Chen Emperor Xuan agreed and thereupon sent envoys on a formal visit.
value.literal: Emperor Xuan of Chen agreed and thereupon sent envoys to pay a court visit.

value.zh: 行本，璠兄子也。
value.en: Xingben was the son of Fan's elder brother.
value.literal: Xingben was Fan's elder brother's son.

value.zh: 父環，仕梁，曆職清顯。
value.en: His father Huan served Liang and successively held clear, eminent posts.
value.literal: His father Huan served Liang and successively held clear, eminent posts.

value.zh: 行本起家梁武陵王國常侍。
value.en: Xingben first entered office as Regular Attendant of the Princely Domain of Wuling of Liang.
value.literal: Xingben first took office as Regular Attendant of the Princely Domain of Wuling of Liang.

value.zh: 遇蕭脩以梁州北附，遂與叔父璠歸周，寓居新豐。
value.en: When Xiao Xiu brought Liang Province north to submit, he returned to Zhou together with his uncle Fan and made his home in Xinfeng.
value.literal: When Xiao Xiu brought Liang Province north to submit, he then returned to Zhou together with his uncle Fan and lodged in Xinfeng.

value.zh: 每以諷讀為事，精力忘疲，雖衣食乏絕，晏如也。
value.en: He always made recitation and reading his occupation, driving himself without fatigue; though food and clothing ran short, he remained perfectly at ease.
value.literal: He always made recitation and reading his occupation, forgetting fatigue in his energy; though food and clothing were exhausted, he was perfectly at ease.

value.zh: 性剛烈，有不可奪之志。
value.en: By nature he was stern and resolute, with a will that could not be wrested away.
value.literal: By nature he was stern and resolute, with a will that could not be wrested away.

value.zh: 周大塚宰宇文護引為中外府記室。
value.en: Yuwen Hu, Grand Minister of Zhou, summoned him as Master of Records of the Central and Outer Headquarters.
value.literal: Yuwen Hu, Grand Minister of Zhou, summoned him as Master of Records of the Central and Outer Headquarters.

value.zh: 武帝親總萬機，轉禦正中士，兼領起居注。
value.en: When Emperor Wu personally took charge of all affairs, Xingben was transferred to Senior Clerk of the Imperial Secretariat and concurrently put in charge of the Daily Record.
value.literal: When Emperor Wu personally took charge of all affairs, Xingben was transferred to Senior Clerk of the Imperial Secretariat and concurrently put in charge of the Daily Record.

value.zh: 累遷掌朝下大夫。
value.en: He was repeatedly promoted to Grand Master of Court Attendance.
value.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Grand Master of Court Attendance.

value.zh: 周代故事，天子臨軒，掌朝典筆硯，持至御坐，則承禦大夫取進之。
value.en: By Zhou custom, when the Son of Heaven faced the hall, the Court Attendance Master held the brush and inkstone and, on reaching the imperial seat, the Assistant Master of Attendance took them and presented them.
value.literal: By Zhou custom, when the Son of Heaven faced the hall, the Court Attendance Master held the brush and inkstone and, when he reached the imperial seat, the Assistant Master of Attendance took them and presented them.

value.zh: 及行本為掌朝，將進筆於帝，承禦復欲取之。
value.en: When Xingben was Court Attendance Master and was about to present the brush to the Emperor, the Assistant Master again tried to take it.
value.literal: When Xingben was Court Attendance Master and was about to present the brush to the Emperor, the Assistant Master again wished to take it.

value.zh: 行本抗聲曰：「筆不可得。」
value.en: Xingben said loudly, "The brush cannot be taken".
value.literal: Xingben said loudly: "The brush cannot be taken".

value.zh: 帝驚視問之，行本曰：「臣聞設官分職，各有司存。
value.en: The Emperor looked up in surprise and asked why; Xingben said, "I have heard that in establishing offices one divides duties, and each has its keeper.
value.literal: The Emperor looked up in surprise and asked why; Xingben said: "I have heard that in establishing offices one divides duties, and each has its keeper.

value.zh: 臣既不得佩承禦刀，承禦亦焉得取臣筆？」
value.en: Since I may not wear the Assistant Master's knife at my belt, how may the Assistant Master take my brush?"
value.literal: Since I may not wear the Assistant Master's knife at my belt, how may the Assistant Master take my brush?"

value.zh: 帝曰：「然。」
value.en: The Emperor said, "So it is."
value.literal: The Emperor said: "So it is."

value.zh: 因令二司各行所職。
value.en: He therefore ordered the two offices each to perform its own duty.
value.literal: He therefore ordered the two offices each to perform its own duty.

value.zh: 及宣帝嗣位，多失德，行本切諫忤旨，出為河內太守。
value.en: When Emperor Xuan succeeded to the throne and often lost virtue, Xingben remonstrated sharply and offended the imperial will; he was sent out as Administrator of Henei.
value.literal: When Emperor Xuan succeeded to the throne and often lost virtue, Xingben remonstrated sharply and offended the imperial will; he was sent out as Administrator of Henei.

value.zh: 及尉遲迥作亂，攻懷州，行本率吏人拒之，拜儀同，賜爵文安縣子。
value.en: When Wei Chijiong rebelled and attacked Huaizhou, Xingben led clerks and people to resist him; he was granted ceremonial parity and enfeoffed as Viscount of Wen'an.
value.literal: When Wei Chijiong rebelled and attacked Huaizhou, Xingben led clerks and people to resist him; he was appointed with ceremonial parity and enfeoffed as Viscount of Wen'an.

value.zh: 儒林下
value.en: Confucian Scholars, Part Two
value.literal: Confucian Scholars, Part Two.

value.zh: 保定三年，盛營宮室。
value.en: In the third year of Baoding palace construction was carried out on a grand scale.
value.literal: In the third year of Baoding, palace buildings were constructed on a grand scale.

value.zh: 春夏大旱，詔公卿百僚，極言得失。
value.en: Spring and summer brought severe drought; the throne ordered ministers and officials to speak freely on what was going wrong.
value.literal: In spring and summer there was great drought; an edict ordered the high ministers and the hundred officials to speak to the utmost on gains and losses.

value.zh: 季明上封事曰：
value.en: Jiming submitted a sealed memorial:
value.literal: Jiming submitted a sealed memorial, saying:

value.zh: 臣聞成湯遭旱，以六事自陳。
value.en: I have heard that when Cheng Tang encountered drought, he confessed his faults in six matters.
value.literal: Your servant has heard that when Cheng Tang encountered drought, he confessed himself in six matters.

value.zh: 宣王太甚，而圭璧斯竭。
value.en: When King Xuan of Zhou went too far, even jade offerings were exhausted.
value.literal: When King Xuan went too far, jade disks and bi were exhausted.

value.zh: 豈非遠慮元元，俯哀黎庶。
value.en: Surely that was because he looked to the welfare of the people and pitied the masses.
value.literal: Was this not because he looked far to the common people and bowed in pity to the masses?

value.zh: 今農要之月，時雨猶愆，率土之心，有懷渴仰。
value.en: Now in the month when agriculture matters most, timely rain is still lacking, and the whole realm looks up in thirst.
value.literal: Now in the month when agriculture is vital, timely rain is still lacking; the heart of all within the realm thirsts and looks up.

value.zh: 陛下垂情萬類，子愛群生，覲禮百神，猶未豐洽。
value.en: Your Majesty cares for all living things and loves the people as his children; you perform rites to the spirits, yet blessings are not yet complete.
value.literal: Your Majesty extends affection to the ten thousand kinds and loves the multitude as children; you observe rites toward the hundred spirits, yet abundance is not yet full.

value.zh: 豈或作事不節，有違時令，舉措失中，當邀斯旱。
value.en: Could it be that undertakings are ill timed, the seasons violated, or measures misplaced, and so this drought has been invited?
value.literal: Could it be that works are not regulated, the seasons are violated, or measures are misplaced, perchance inviting this drought?

value.zh: 《春秋》，君舉必書，動為典禮。
value.en: The Spring and Autumn Annals records every act of a ruler; conduct is canon and ritual.
value.literal: The Spring and Autumn Annals records that a ruler's every act must be written; movement is canon and ritual.

value.zh: 水旱陰陽，莫不應行而至。
value.en: Flood, drought, and the balance of yin and yang all respond to how a ruler behaves.
value.literal: Flood, drought, yin and yang—none fail to respond to conduct and arrive.

value.zh: 孔子曰：「言行，君子之所以動天地，可不慎乎！」
value.en: Confucius said, "Words and conduct are how the gentleman moves Heaven and Earth—can one not be cautious?"
value.literal: Confucius said, "Words and conduct are how the gentleman moves Heaven and Earth—can one not be cautious?"

value.zh: 《春秋》莊公三十一年冬，不雨，《五行傳》以為是歲一年而三築台，奢侈不恤人也。
value.en: The Spring and Autumn Annals records that in the thirty-first year of Duke Zhuang of Lu, winter, there was no rain. The Treatise on the Five Phases holds that in that year three platforms were built in one year—extravagance without pity for the people.
value.literal: The Spring and Autumn Annals, Duke Zhuang year 31 winter: no rain. The Treatise on the Five Phases holds that in that year platforms were built three times in one year—extravagance without pity for the people.

value.zh: 僖公二十一年夏，大旱，《五行傳》以為時作南門，勞人興役。
value.en: In the twenty-first year of Duke Xi of Lu, summer, there was great drought. The Treatise on the Five Phases holds that at that time the southern gate was under construction, exhausting the people with labor.
value.literal: Duke Xi year 21 summer: great drought. The Treatise on the Five Phases holds that at that time the southern gate was being built, laboring the people with corvée.

value.zh: 漢惠帝二年夏，大旱，五年夏，大旱，江河水少，溪澗水絕，《五行傳》以為先是發十四萬六千人城長安。
value.en: In the second year of Emperor Hui of Han, summer, there was great drought. In the fifth year, summer, there was great drought; the great rivers ran low and streams dried up. The Treatise on the Five Phases holds that before this 146,000 men had been mobilized to build the walls of Chang'an.
value.literal: Emperor Hui of Han year 2 summer: great drought. Year 5 summer: great drought; the Yangtze and Yellow rivers had little water, and streams and brooks dried up. The Treatise on the Five Phases holds that before this 146,000 men had been mobilized to build the walls of Chang'an.

value.zh: 漢武帝元狩三年夏，大旱，《五行傳》以為是歲發天下故吏，穿昆明池。
value.en: In the third year of Yuanshou of Emperor Wu of Han, summer, there was great drought. The Treatise on the Five Phases holds that in that year former officials throughout the realm were mobilized to dig the Kunming Pool.
value.literal: Emperor Wu of Han, Yuanshou year 3 summer: great drought. The Treatise on the Five Phases holds that in that year men throughout the realm who had formerly held office were mobilized to dig the Kunming Pool.

value.zh: 然則土木之功，動人興役，天輒應之以異。
value.en: Thus whenever earth and wood works mobilize the people, Heaven responds with anomalies.
value.literal: Thus works of earth and wood, moving the people with corvée—Heaven always responds with anomalies.

value.zh: 典籍作誡，倘或可思，上天譴告，改之則善。
value.en: The warnings of the classics are perhaps worth pondering; Heaven's reproof, if heeded, leads to good.
value.literal: The admonitions of the classics—perhaps they may be pondered; Heaven's reproof—if changed, then good.

value.zh: 今若息人省役，以答天譴，庶靈澤時降，嘉谷有時，則年登可覬，子來非晚。
value.en: If Your Majesty now rests the people and reduces corvée to answer Heaven's reproof, timely rain may fall, grain ripen, and the people come gladly—not too late.
value.literal: If now the people are rested and corvée reduced, to answer Heaven's reproof, then perhaps timely blessings will descend, fine grain will ripen in season, the year's harvest may be hoped for, and the people will come as children—not late.

value.zh: 《詩》云：「人亦勞止，迄可小康，惠此中國，以綏四方。」
value.en: The Odes say, "The people also have labored; let them have a little ease; show favor to this central kingdom to bring peace to the four quarters."
value.literal: The Odes say, "The people also have labored; let them have a little ease; show favor to this central kingdom to bring peace to the four quarters."

value.zh: 或恐極陽生陰，秋多雨水，年復不登，人將無覬。
value.en: Or perhaps when yang reaches its extreme, yin will arise; autumn may bring heavy rain, the harvest may fail again, and the people will have nothing to hope for.
value.literal: Or perhaps one fears that when yang reaches its extreme yin is born, and in autumn there will be much rain; the year again will not yield, and the people will have nothing to hope for.

value.zh: 如又薦饑，為慮更甚。
value.en: If famine follows as well, the danger is even greater.
value.literal: If famine is added on top, the concern is even greater.

value.zh: 臣聞寬大所以兼覆，慈愛所以懷眾。
value.en: I have heard that breadth enables covering all, and kindness enables embracing the multitude.
value.literal: Your servant has heard that breadth and largeness are what enable covering all; kindness and love are what enable embracing the multitude.

value.zh: 故天地稱其高厚者，萬物得其容養焉；
value.en: Heaven and Earth are called high and thick because the ten thousand things receive shelter and nurture from them;
value.literal: Therefore Heaven and Earth are called high and thick because the ten thousand things receive their shelter and nurture;

value.zh: 四時著其寒暑者，庶類資其忠信焉。
value.en: the four seasons show cold and heat because all living kinds rely on their constancy and good faith.
value.literal: the four seasons display their cold and heat because the myriad kinds rely on their constancy and trust.

value.zh: 是以帝王者，寬大象天地，忠信則四時。
value.en: Thus emperors and kings model themselves on the breadth of Heaven and Earth and the good faith of the four seasons.
value.literal: Thus emperors and kings take Heaven and Earth as their model of breadth, and the four seasons as their constancy and trust.

value.zh: 招搖東指，天下識其春；
value.en: When the Dipper points east, all under Heaven knows spring has come;
value.literal: When the Dipper points east, all under Heaven knows it is spring;

value.zh: 人君布德，率土懷其惠。
value.en: when a ruler spreads virtue, the realm cherishes his grace.
value.literal: when a ruler spreads virtue, all within the realm cherishes his grace.

value.zh: 伏惟陛下，資乾禦宇，品物咸亨，時乘六龍，自強不息，好問受規，天下幸甚。
value.en: Your Majesty, endowed with Heaven's potency, governs all things in prosperity, rides the six dragons without cease, and loves to ask and receive remonstrance—the realm is greatly blessed.
value.literal: Bow low: Your Majesty, endowed with Heaven's potency, governs the universe; all things flourish. You ride the six dragons, strengthen yourself without cease, love to ask and receive remonstrance—the realm is greatly blessed.

value.zh: 自古至道之君，亦皆廣延博訪，詢采皞蕘，置鼓樹木，以求其過。
value.en: Since antiquity rulers of utmost virtue have sought counsel widely, even from the humblest, and welcomed criticism to learn their faults.
value.literal: From antiquity the rulers of utmost Way have all broadly extended invitations and sought counsel, gathering even the words of grass cutters, setting up drums and trees to welcome criticism, to seek out their faults.

value.zh: 頃者亢旱逾時，人懷望歲，陛下爰發明詔，廣求六瘼，同禹、湯之罪己，高宋景之守正，澍雨應時，年穀斯稔。
value.en: In recent years drought lasted beyond its season and the people hoped for rain. Your Majesty issued a brilliant edict seeking the people's afflictions, matching Yu and Tang in blaming yourself and Duke Jing of Song in holding to the upright; timely rain came and the year's grain ripened.
value.literal: In recent years drought lasted beyond its season; people harbored hope for the year's harvest. Your Majesty then issued a brilliant edict, broadly seeking the six afflictions of the people, matching Yu and Tang in blaming themselves and rising to Duke Jing of Song in holding to the upright; timely rain responded, and the year's grain ripened.

value.zh: 克己節用，慕質去華，此則尚矣。
value.en: You restrained yourself and economized, admired simplicity and detested extravagance—this is already lofty.
value.literal: Restraining oneself and economizing, admiring simplicity and detesting splendor—this is already lofty.

value.zh: 然而硃紫仍耀于衢路，綺縠猶侈于豪富，短褐未充於細人，糟糠未厭於編戶。
value.en: Yet crimson and purple still blaze on the roads, fine silks still adorn wealthy houses, coarse cloth does not clothe the common people, and coarse grain does not fill their bowls.
value.literal: Yet crimson and purple still blaze on the roads, and fine silks are still extravagant in wealthy houses; coarse cloth does not fill the common people, and chaff and husks do not satisfy registered households.

value.zh: 此則勸導之理，有所未周故也。
value.en: This shows that guidance and persuasion have not yet reached everywhere.
value.literal: This is because the principle of guidance and leading has not yet been fully applied.

value.zh: 今雖導之以禮，齊之以刑，風俗固難以一矣。
value.en: Though you guide them with ritual and align them with punishments, custom is hard to unify at once.
value.literal: Now though you guide them with ritual and align them with punishments, custom is hard to make one.

value.zh: 昔漢文帝集上書之囊，以作帷帳；
value.en: Formerly Emperor Wen of Han gathered memorial bags to make curtains;
value.literal: Formerly Emperor Wen of Han gathered the bags of memorials to make curtains;

value.zh: 惜十家之產，不造露臺。
value.en: he would not build a terrace that cost the wealth of ten households;
value.literal: he prized the wealth of ten households and would not build the open terrace;

value.zh: 後宮所幸，衣不曳地，方之今日富室之飾，嘗不如婢隸之服。
value.en: palace women wore robes that did not trail on the ground—compared with rich houses today, even servants dress more lavishly.
value.literal: those favored in the rear palace wore robes that did not trail on the ground—compared with the adornment of rich houses today, they were not even like servants' dress.

value.zh: 然而以身率下，國富刑清，廟稱太宗，良有以也。
value.en: By leading through his own example the state grew rich and punishments were clear; the temple honors him as Emperor Taizong, and rightly so.
value.literal: Yet by taking the body to lead those below, the state grew rich and punishments were clear; the temple calls him Emperor Taizong—and rightly so.

value.zh: 臣聞聖人久于其道而天下化成。
value.en: When the sage long abides in the Way, all under Heaven is transformed.
value.literal: Your servant has heard that when the sage long abides in the Way, all under Heaven is transformed.

value.zh: 今承魏氏衰亂之後，貞信未興。
value.en: Now, after the disorders of Wei, constancy and trust have not yet been restored.
value.literal: Now, inheriting the age after Wei's disorders, constancy and trust have not yet arisen.

value.zh: 宜先尊五美，屏四惡，革浮華之俗，抑流競之風，察鴻都之小藝，焚雉頭之異服，無益之貨勿重于時，虧德之器勿陳於側，則人知德矣。
value.en: First follow the five beauties and banish the four evils: reform empty display, restrain reckless competition, examine minor arts, burn outlandish dress, let useless goods not be prized, and harmful luxuries not be displayed—then the people will know virtue.
value.literal: One should first follow the five beauties and banish the four evils, reform the custom of empty show, restrain the wind of reckless competition, examine the minor arts of Hongdu, burn the strange garments of pheasant-head style, let goods of no benefit not be prized in the age, and vessels that harm virtue not be displayed at the side—then the people will know virtue.

value.zh: 帝覽而嘉之。
value.en: The emperor read the memorial and commended him.
value.literal: The emperor read it and commended him.

value.zh: 卷五十二 竇田灌韓傳第二十二
value.en: Volume 52: Biographies of Dou, Tian, Guan, and Han (Part 22).
value.literal: Volume 52: Biographies of Dou, Tian, Guan, and Han, number twenty-two.

value.zh: 嬰銳為救夫，嬰夫人諫曰：「灌將軍得罪丞相，與太后家迕，寧可救邪？」
value.en: Dou Ying was bent on saving Guan Fu. His wife warned him, "Guan Fu has insulted the chancellor and defied the Tian family—can you save him?"
value.literal: Ying was keen to save Fu; Ying's wife remonstrated, saying, "General Guan has offended the chancellor and crossed the empress dowager's house—can he possibly be saved?"

value.zh: 嬰曰：「侯自我得之，自我捐之，無所恨。
value.en: Dou Ying said, "I won my title with my own merit; I may lose it the same way—I have no regrets.
value.literal: Ying said, "The marquisate I won for myself I may cast away for myself; I have no regret.

value.zh: 且終不令灌仲孺獨死，嬰獨生。」
value.en: Nor will I let Guan Zhongru die while I alone survive."
value.literal: Moreover in the end I will not allow Guan Zhongru to die alone while I, Ying, live."

value.zh: 乃匿其家，竊出上書。
value.en: He slipped past his household, stole out, and filed a memorial with the throne.
value.literal: Thereupon he hid it from his family, stole out, and submitted a memorial.

value.zh: 立召人，具告言灌夫醉飽事，不足誅。
value.en: He had Guan Fu brought in at once and laid out the whole drunken-scene story, arguing it did not merit death.
value.literal: He immediately summoned a man in and fully reported Guan Fu's drunken surfeit affair, saying it did not merit execution.

value.zh: 上然之，賜嬰食，曰：「東朝廷辯之。」
value.en: The emperor assented, fed Dou Ying, and said, "Argue it out in the eastern court."
value.literal: The emperor agreed, gave Ying a meal, and said, "Debate it in the eastern court."

value.zh: 嬰東朝，盛推夫善，言其醉飽得過，乃丞相以它事誣罪之。
value.en: At the eastern court Dou Ying praised Guan Fu to the skies, blamed the brawl on drink, and called Tian Fen's charges a frame-up.
value.literal: Ying went to the eastern court and greatly praised Fu's goodness, saying his offense was drunken surfeit, and that the chancellor had falsely accused him on other matters.

value.zh: 蚡盛毀夫所為橫恣，罪逆不道。
value.en: Tian Fen blackened Guan Fu as a bully whose crimes knew no law.
value.literal: Fen greatly slandered Fu's conduct as violent and arbitrary, criminal and contrary to the Way.

value.zh: 嬰度無可奈何，因言蚡短。
value.en: Seeing he was losing, Dou Ying turned to Tian Fen's own faults.
value.literal: Ying, estimating there was nothing to be done, therefore spoke of Fen's shortcomings.

value.zh: 蚡曰：「天下幸而安樂無事，蚡得為肺附，所好音樂、狗馬、田宅，所愛倡優、巧匠之屬，不如魏其、灌夫日夜招聚天下豪傑壯士與論議，腹誹而心謗，卬視天，俯畫地，辟睨兩官間，幸天下有變，而欲有大功。
value.en: Tian Fen said, "While the empire enjoys peace, I, as the emperor's uncle, care for music, hounds, horses, and mansions—singers, actors, and craftsmen. I am nothing like Dou Ying and Guan Fu, who recruit ruffians day and night, nurse private grudges, scan heaven and earth, and leer toward both palaces, praying for turmoil so they can seize glory.
value.literal: Fen said, "So long as the realm is fortunate enough to be at peace and without incident, I, Fen, have been able to be kin to the throne; what I love are music, dogs, horses, fields, and houses; what I cherish are singers, actors, and clever craftsmen—I am not like Marquis of Weiqi and Guan Fu, who day and night gather the bold spirits and stalwarts of the realm to debate with them, who slander in the belly and revile in the heart, who look up to mark the sky and look down to trace the earth, who squint between the two palaces, hoping the realm will meet with change so they may win great merit.

value.zh: 臣乃不如魏其等所為。」
value.en: I am not in their league."
value.literal: I am indeed not equal to what Marquis of Weiqi and the others do."

value.zh: 上問朝臣：「兩人孰是？」
value.en: The emperor asked his ministers, "Who speaks truth?"
value.literal: The emperor asked the court ministers, "Which of the two is right?"

value.zh: 御史大夫韓安國曰：「魏其言灌夫父死事，身荷戟馳不測之吳軍，身被數十創，名冠三軍，此天下壯士，非有大惡，爭杯酒，不足引它過以誅也。
value.en: Han Anguo said, "Dou Ying is right that Guan Fu's father died in battle while the son, halberd in hand, charged the Wu lines and took dozens of wounds—a hero of the empire. Without a graver crime than a wine quarrel, he should not die for it.
value.literal: Censor-in-chief Han Anguo said, "As Marquis of Weiqi says, Guan Fu's father died in service; he himself shouldered a halberd and galloped into the immeasurable Wu army, his body suffering dozens of wounds; his fame crowned the three armies—he is a stalwart of the realm. Unless he has committed some great evil, to wring another fault from a quarrel over cups of wine is not enough ground for execution.

value.zh: 魏其言是。
value.en: Marquis Dou speaks the truth.
value.literal: What Marquis of Weiqi says is correct.

value.zh: 丞相亦言灌夫通姦猾，侵細民，家累巨萬，橫恣穎川，□轢宗室，侵犯骨肉，此所謂『支大於干，脛大於股，不折必披』。
value.en: The chancellor is also right: Guan Fu consorts with villains, preys on the weak, has piled up a fortune, tyrannizes Yingchuan, rides roughshod over the imperial clan, and wrongs his own blood—what the proverb calls a limb thicker than the trunk, a calf thicker than the thigh: something must snap.
value.literal: The chancellor also says that Guan Fu associates with crafty scoundrels, bullies the common people, his household wealth piles to vast sums, he runs riot in Yingchuan, tramples the imperial house, and violates flesh-and-blood kin—this is what is called "when the branch is greater than the trunk, when the shin is greater than the thigh, if it does not break it will split."

value.zh: 丞相信亦是。
value.en: The chancellor speaks truth as well.
value.literal: What the chancellor says is also correct.

value.zh: 唯明主裁之。」
value.en: Only Your Majesty can judge."
value.literal: Let the enlightened ruler decide."

value.zh: 主爵都尉汲黯是魏其。
value.en: Ji An, chief commandant of the nobility, backed Dou Ying.
value.literal: Chief Commandant of the Nobility Ji An sided with Marquis of Weiqi.

value.zh: 內史鄭當時是魏其，後不堅。
value.en: Palace secretary Zheng Dangshi began on Dou Ying's side, then wavered.
value.literal: Palace Secretary Zheng Dangshi sided with Marquis of Weiqi, but later did not hold firm.

value.zh: 餘皆莫敢對。
value.en: The others held their tongues.
value.literal: The rest all dared not answer.

value.zh: 上怒內史曰：「公平生數言魏其、武安長短，今日廷論，局趣效轅下駒，吾並斬若屬矣！」
value.en: The emperor turned on Zheng Dangshi: "You have spent years weighing Dou Ying against Tian Fen; today at court you freeze like a colt between the traces—I could behead you all!"
value.literal: The emperor grew angry at the palace secretary and said, "You, sir, have all your life often spoken of the strengths and weaknesses of Marquis of Weiqi and Marquis of Wu'an; today at court debate you are cramped and act like a colt under the shafts—I will behead the lot of you!"

value.zh: 即罷起入，上食太后。
value.en: He cut the session short, rose, and withdrew to dine with his mother.
value.literal: Immediately he stopped, rose, and entered; he took his meal with the empress dowager.

value.zh: 太后亦已使人候司，具以語太后。
value.en: She had already posted spies; they told her everything.
value.literal: The empress dowager had already sent someone to watch and report; they fully told the empress dowager.

value.zh: 太后怒，不食，曰：「我在也，而人皆藉吾弟，令我百歲後，皆魚肉之乎！
value.en: She refused her meal in fury: "I am still alive, yet they walk on my brother; when I am gone, will they cut him to pieces?
value.literal: The empress dowager was angry, would not eat, and said, "While I am still alive, they all trample my younger brother; after I reach a hundred years, will they carve him up like fish meat!

value.zh: 且帝寧能為石人邪！
value.en: And is the emperor a block of stone, deaf to his own mother?
value.literal: Moreover can the emperor really be a stone man!

value.zh: 此特帝在，即錄錄，設百歲後，是屬寧有可信者乎？」
value.en: Only while you sit on the throne do they cringe; once you are gone, would you trust a single one of them?"
value.literal: This is only while the emperor is alive that they are submissive and timid; suppose after a hundred years—can any of this lot be trusted?"

value.zh: 上謝曰：「俱外家，故廷辨之。
value.en: The emperor apologized: "Both sides are my in-laws—that is why I aired the dispute in open court.
value.literal: The emperor apologized and said, "They are both maternal kin, therefore I debated them at court.

value.zh: 不然，此一獄吏所決耳。」
value.en: Otherwise a county jailer could have settled it."
value.literal: If not for that, this would be something a single jail clerk could decide."

value.zh: 是時，郎中令石建為上分別言兩人。
value.en: Supervisor of the household Shi Jian then gave the emperor a private briefing on each man.
value.literal: At that time the supervisor of the household Shi Jian separately explained the two men to the emperor.

value.zh: 於是上使御史簿責嬰所言灌夫頗不讎，劾繫都司空。
value.en: The emperor had the censor cross-examine Dou Ying: his claims about Guan Fu did not check out; he was impeached and jailed under the metropolitan superintendent.
value.literal: Thereupon the emperor ordered the censor to register and call Ying to account for what he had said about Guan Fu, which largely did not match; he impeached him and bound him in the metropolitan superintendent's custody.

value.zh: 孝景時，嬰嘗受遺詔，曰「事有不便，以便宜論上」。
value.en: Emperor Jing had once given Dou Ying a sealed rescript: "If state business goes awry, memorialize as you see fit."
value.literal: Under Emperor Jing, Ying had once received a testamentary edict saying, "If affairs are inconvenient, you may memorialize at your discretion on what is advantageous."

value.zh: 及系，灌夫罪至族，事日急，諸公莫敢復明言於上。
value.en: By then Guan Fu faced extermination of his clan; the case raced toward verdict, and no minister dared speak for Dou Ying at court.
value.literal: By the time he was bound, Guan Fu's crime reached to clan extermination; the affair grew urgent daily, and no grandee dared speak plainly again to the emperor.

value.zh: 嬰乃使昆弟子上書言之，幸得召見。
value.en: Dou Ying smuggled a memorial out through a nephew, hoping for a summons.
value.literal: Ying then had a nephew submit a memorial on it, hoping to obtain an audience.

value.zh: 書奏，案尚書，大行無遺詔。
value.en: When the memorial arrived, the imperial secretariat searched its records but found no such testamentary edict from the late emperor.
value.literal: When the memorial was presented, they examined the secretariat records and found no such testamentary edict from the late emperor.

value.zh: 詔書獨臧嬰家，嬰家丞封。
value.en: The only copy of the alleged edict had lain in Dou Ying's house under his steward's seal.
value.literal: The edict text alone was stored in Ying's house; Ying's household steward had sealed it.

value.zh: 乃劾嬰矯先帝詔害，罪當棄市。
value.en: He was charged with forging a dead emperor's edict—a capital offense.
value.literal: Thereupon they impeached Ying for forging the late emperor's edict to do harm; the crime merited execution in the market.

value.zh: 五年十月，悉論灌夫支屬。
value.en: In the tenth month of the fifth year the entire Guan clan was condemned.
value.literal: In the tenth month of the fifth year, they sentenced all branches of Guan Fu's kin.

value.zh: 嬰良久乃聞有劾，即陽病痱，不食慾死。
value.en: Dou Ying learned of the impeachment late; he feigned a stroke, refused food, and prepared to die.
value.literal: Only after a long time did Ying hear of the impeachment; then he feigned apoplexy, would not eat, and wished to die.

value.zh: 或聞上無意殺嬰，復食，治病，議定不死矣。
value.en: Word spread that the emperor would spare him; he took food again, nursed his health, and his friends thought he was safe.
value.literal: Some heard that the emperor had no intention of killing Ying; he ate again, treated his illness, and they reckoned he would surely not die.

value.zh: 乃有飛語為惡言聞上，故以十二月晦論棄市渭城。
value.en: Then anonymous slander reached the throne; on the last day of the twelfth month he was ordered executed at Weicheng market.
value.literal: Then flying rumors of evil words reached the emperor; therefore on the last day of the twelfth month he was sentenced to execution in the market at Weicheng.

value.zh: 春，蚡疾，一身盡痛，若有擊者，呼服謝罪。
value.en: That spring Tian Fen fell ill, racked with pains as from blows, screaming confessions and pleas for mercy.
value.literal: In spring Fen fell ill; his whole body ached as if struck; he cried out that he submitted and begged pardon.

value.zh: 上使視鬼者瞻之，曰：「魏其侯與灌夫共守，笞欲殺之。」
value.en: The emperor sent a spirit-medium, who reported, "Marquis Dou and Guan Fu stand over him, flogging him to death."
value.literal: The emperor had one who could see ghosts examine him; he said, "Marquis of Weiqi and Guan Fu together guard him, beating him with sticks and wishing to kill him."

value.zh: 竟死。
value.en: He died.
value.literal: In the end he died.

value.zh: 子恬嗣，元朔中有罪免。
value.en: His son Tian inherited the title but lost it to a crime in Yuanshuo.
value.literal: His son Tian succeeded; during Yuanshuo he committed a crime and was dismissed.

value.zh: 後淮南王安謀反，覺。
value.en: Later Liu An, king of Huainan, rebelled; the plot was exposed.
value.literal: Later the King of Huainan, Liu An, plotted rebellion; it was discovered.

value.zh: 始安入朝時，蚡為太尉，迎安霸上，謂安曰：「上未有太子，大王最賢，高祖孫，即宮車晏駕，非大王立，尚誰立哉？」
value.en: On Liu An's first visit to court, Tian Fen—then grand commandant—met him at Bashang and said, "The throne has no heir; you are Gaozu's ablest grandson; when the emperor dies, if anyone mounts the throne but you, who should it be?"
value.literal: When An first entered court for an audience, Fen was grand commandant; he welcomed An at Bashang and said to An, "The emperor has not yet established an heir apparent; you, great king, are the worthiest, a grandson of Gaozu; when the imperial carriage is delayed in setting out, if not you, great king, who is established, who else could be?"

value.zh: 淮南王大喜，厚遺金錢財物。
value.en: The king of Huainan was delighted and showered him with gold and treasure.
value.literal: The King of Huainan was greatly pleased and richly presented gold, cash, and goods.

value.zh: 上自嬰、夫事時不直蚡，特為太后故。
value.en: Throughout the Dou–Guan affair the emperor had judged Tian Fen in the wrong but indulged him for his mother's sake.
value.literal: From the time of the affair of Ying and Fu the emperor had not thought Fen in the right, but only for the empress dowager's sake.

value.zh: 及聞淮南事，上曰：「使武安侯在者，族矣。」
value.en: When the Huainan case broke, the emperor said, "If Tian Fen still lived, I would exterminate his whole line."
value.literal: When he heard of the Huainan affair, the emperor said, "If Marquis of Wu'an were still alive, he would have been exterminated to the clan."

value.zh: 梁王以至親故，得自置相、二千石，出入遊戲，僭於天子。
value.en: As the emperor's brother, the king of Liang could name his own chancellor and two-thousand-picul officials; his comings and goings aped the imperial style.
value.literal: Because the King of Liang was close kin, he was permitted to appoint his own chancellor and officials at two thousand piculs; in going out and coming in for sport he exceeded the Son of Heaven.

value.zh: 天子聞之，心不善。
value.en: The emperor heard of it and took offense.
value.literal: When the Son of Heaven heard of it, his heart was not pleased.

value.zh: 太后知帝弗善，乃怒梁使者，弗見，案責王所為。
value.en: The empress dowager knew her son disapproved; she snubbed Liang's messengers and demanded an accounting of the king's behavior.
value.literal: The empress dowager knew the emperor did not approve; she then grew angry at Liang's envoys, would not receive them, and investigated and called the king to account for his conduct.

value.zh: 安國為梁使，見大長公主而泣曰：「何梁王為人子之孝，為人臣之忠，而太后曾不省也？
value.en: Han Anguo, speaking for Liang, wept before the grand princess: "The king is a dutiful son and a loyal vassal—why will the empress dowager not see it?
value.literal: Anguo, as Liang's envoy, saw the grand princess and wept, saying, "How is it that the King of Liang, as a son, is filial, as a minister is loyal, yet the empress dowager never examines this?

value.zh: 夫前日吳、楚、齊、趙七國反，自關以東皆合從而西向，唯梁最親，為限難。
value.en: When the seven kingdoms rose east of the passes and turned their spears westward, only Liang—closest of kin—bore the brunt.
value.literal: The other day when Wu, Chu, Qi, Zhao, and the seven states rebelled, from the passes east all joined in a vertical alliance and faced west; only Liang was closest kin and formed the hard barrier.

value.zh: 梁王念太后、帝在中，而諸侯擾亂，壹言泣數行而下，跪送臣等六人將兵擊卻吳、楚、吳、楚以故兵不敢西，而卒破亡，梁之力也。
value.en: With the realm in chaos he thought only of you and the emperor; tears streamed at a single word; he knelt and sent six of us with an army that pinned Wu and Chu so they never marched west—that broke the rebellion.
value.literal: The King of Liang thought of the empress dowager and the emperor amid them while the marquises were in turmoil; with one word his tears fell in several streams; he knelt and sent us six men with troops to strike back Wu and Chu; for this reason Wu and Chu did not dare go west, and in the end were broken and destroyed—the strength was Liang's.

value.zh: 今太后以小苛禮責望梁王。
value.en: Now you fault him for petty breaches of etiquette.
value.literal: Now the empress dowager blames and expects the King of Liang over petty matters of ritual.

value.zh: 梁王父兄皆帝王，而所見者大，故出稱蹕，入言警，車旗皆帝所賜，即以□鄙小縣，驅馳國中，欲誇諸侯，令天下知太后、帝愛之也。
value.en: Raised among emperors, he thinks in large scale: he speaks of imperial escort and cordons because his equipage was all your gift; even on a tour of a minor county he parades the kingdom so all may see how you and the emperor cherish him.
value.literal: The King of Liang's father and elder brothers were all emperors, and what he has seen is great; therefore when he goes out he speaks of clearing the way, when he enters he speaks of precautions; chariots and banners were all gifts from the emperor—even in this petty commandery he gallops through the state, wishing to boast to the marquises and let the realm know the empress dowager and the emperor love him.

value.zh: 今梁使來，輒案責之，梁王恐，日夜滋泣思慕，不知所為。
value.en: Yet every Liang messenger is hauled in for interrogation; the king lives in terror, weeping day and night, unsure what to do.
value.literal: Now whenever Liang's envoys come, you always investigate and call them to account; the King of Liang is afraid, day and night weeps and longs in thought, and does not know what to do.

value.zh: 何梁王之忠孝而太后不恤也？」
value.en: How can he be so loyal and filial while you withhold your mercy?"
value.literal: How can the King of Liang be loyal and filial while the empress dowager shows no pity?"

value.zh: 長公主具以告太后，太后喜曰：「為帝言之。」
value.en: The grand princess repeated every word; the empress dowager beamed and said, "Tell the emperor."
value.literal: The grand princess reported everything to the empress dowager; the empress dowager was pleased and said, "Speak of it to the emperor."

value.zh: 言之，帝心乃解，而免冠謝太后曰：「兄弟不能相教，乃為太后遺憂。」
value.en: She did; the emperor's anger melted. He doffed his cap and apologized to his mother: "We brothers failed each other and caused you grief."
value.literal: When she spoke of it, the emperor's heart was then relieved; he removed his cap and apologized to the empress dowager, saying, "Brothers could not instruct each other, and so caused the empress dowager worry."

value.zh: 悉見梁使，厚賜之。
value.en: He received every Liang envoy and rewarded them generously.
value.literal: He received all Liang's envoys and richly rewarded them.

value.zh: 其後，梁王益親歡。
value.en: Afterward the bond between throne and king of Liang grew warm again.
value.literal: After that, the King of Liang grew ever closer in affection.

value.zh: 太后、長公主更賜安國直千餘金。
value.en: The empress dowager and the grand princess together gave Han Anguo over a thousand cash-weight in gold.
value.literal: The empress dowager and the grand princess additionally bestowed on Anguo more than a thousand in cash weight of gold.

value.zh: 由此顯，結於漢。
value.en: He rose in fame and was tied to the court at Chang'an.
value.literal: From this he became eminent and formed ties with Han.

value.zh: 公孫詭、羊勝說王求為帝太子及益地事，恐漢大臣不聽，乃陰使人刺漢用事謀臣。
value.en: Gongsun Gui and Yang Sheng urged the king to seek the crown princeship and more land; fearing refusal from Chang'an, they hired killers for Han's leading advisers.
value.literal: Gongsun Gui and Yang Sheng persuaded the king to seek to become heir apparent to the emperor and to increase his territory; fearing Han ministers would not consent, they secretly sent men to assassinate influential Han strategists.

value.zh: 及殺故吳相爰盎，景帝遂聞詭、勝等計劃，乃遣使捕詭、勝，必得。
value.en: After they murdered Yuan Ang, the former chancellor of Wu, Emperor Jing learned of the plot and sent men to seize Gongsun Gui and Yang Sheng alive.
value.literal: When they had killed the former chancellor of Wu, Yuan Ang, Emperor Jing eventually learned of Gui and Sheng's plots; he then sent agents to arrest Gui and Sheng, demanding they be taken.

value.zh: 漢使十輩至梁，相以下舉國大索，月餘弗得。
value.en: Ten separate Han delegations searched Liang from chancellor to constable for over a month without success.
value.literal: Han envoys came in ten parties to Liang; from the chancellor down the whole state searched greatly for more than a month without finding them.

value.zh: 安國聞詭、勝匿王所，乃入見王而泣曰：「主辱者臣死。
value.en: Han Anguo learned the two men were hidden in the palace. He entered in tears: "When the lord is dishonored, his servant should die.
value.literal: Anguo heard that Gui and Sheng were hidden at the king's place; he then entered, saw the king, and wept, saying, "When the ruler is shamed, the minister should die.

value.zh: 大王無良臣，故紛紛至此。
value.en: You have no loyal ministers—that is why matters have come to this pass.
value.literal: The great king has no good ministers; therefore it has come to this confusion.

value.zh: 今勝、詭不得，請辭賜死。」
value.en: If those two are not produced, grant me death."
value.literal: Now that Sheng and Gui cannot be obtained, I beg leave to accept a gift of death."

value.zh: 王曰：「何至此？」
value.en: The king said, "How can it be so grave?"
value.literal: The king said, "How has it reached this?"

value.zh: 安國泣數行下，曰：「大王自度於皇帝，孰與太上皇之與高帝及皇帝與臨江王親？」
value.en: Han Anguo wept freely: "Tell me—which bond is tighter: the Grand Supreme Emperor and Gaozu, or the emperor and the prince of Linjiang?"
value.literal: Anguo's tears fell in several streams as he said, "Great king, you yourself measure against the emperor—which is closer, the Grand Supreme Emperor to Gaozu, or the emperor to the Prince of Linjiang?"

value.zh: 王曰：「弗如也。」
value.en: The king said, "I am not as close to the emperor as those pairs were."
value.literal: The king said, "It does not compare."

value.zh: 安國曰：「夫太上皇、臨江親父子間，然高帝曰『提三尺取天下者朕也』，故太上終不得制事，居於櫟陽。
value.en: Han Anguo said: "Gaozu and his father, the emperor and the prince of Linjiang—each was a tight father-son pair—yet Gaozu declared, The sword that won the realm is mine, and the old emperor finished his life powerless at Liyang.
value.literal: Anguo said, "Between the Grand Supreme Emperor and Gaozu, and between the Prince of Linjiang and the emperor—these were close father-and-son bonds—yet Gaozu said, 'He who took the realm with a three-foot sword is I,' so in the end the Grand Supreme could not control affairs and dwelt at Liyang.

value.zh: 臨江，適長太子，以一言過，廢王臨江；
value.en: The prince of Linjiang was the legitimate eldest son; one slip of the tongue cost him his kingdom;
value.literal: Linjiang, as the eldest heir apparent of the proper line, because of one word's fault was deposed as king of Linjiang;

value.zh: 用宮垣事，卒自殺中尉府。
value.en: on a charge about palace walls he ended his life in the metropolitan commandant's yamen.
value.literal: because of the affair of the palace walls, in the end he killed himself in the commandant of the capital's office.

value.zh: 何者？
value.en: Why?
value.literal: Why was it so?

value.zh: 治天下終不用私亂公。
value.en: Because the empire is never ruled by private affection over public law.
value.literal: In ruling the realm one never uses private feeling to disorder the public good.

value.zh: 語曰：『雖有親父，安知不為虎？
value.en: The proverb runs: Even a loving father may prove a tiger;
value.literal: The saying goes, "Though there is a loving father, how do you know he is not a tiger?

value.zh: 雖有親兄，安知不為狼？』
value.en: even a loving brother may prove a wolf."
value.literal: Though there is a loving elder brother, how do you know he is not a wolf?"

value.zh: 今大王列在諸侯，訹邪臣浮說，犯上禁，橈明法。
value.en: You are only a feudal king; venal advisers have led you to break the throne's edicts and warp the code.
value.literal: Now you, great king, are listed among the marquises; seduced by wicked ministers' empty talk, you violate the sovereign's prohibitions and bend the clear law.

value.zh: 天子以太后故，不忍致法於大王。
value.en: The emperor stays his hand only for his mother's sake.
value.literal: The Son of Heaven, for the empress dowager's sake, cannot bear to apply the law to you, great king.

value.zh: 太后日夜涕泣，幸大王自改，大王終不覺寤。
value.en: She weeps day and night for you to mend your ways; you refuse to wake.
value.literal: The empress dowager weeps day and night, hoping you, great king, will reform yourself; you, great king, never wake to it.

value.zh: 有如太后宮車即晏駕，大王尚誰攀乎？」
value.en: When her carriage at last climbs the western slope, whom will you cling to?"
value.literal: Suppose the empress dowager's carriage should be delayed in setting out—whom will you, great king, cling to then?"

value.zh: 語未卒，王泣數行而下，謝安國曰：「吾今出之。」
value.en: Before he finished, the king was sobbing; he thanked Han Anguo and said, "I will hand them over."
value.literal: Before the words were finished, the king's tears fell in several streams; he apologized to Anguo, saying, "I will now release them."

value.zh: 即日詭、勝自殺。
value.en: That day Gongsun Gui and Yang Sheng committed suicide.
value.literal: That same day Gui and Sheng killed themselves.

value.zh: 漢使還報，梁事皆得釋，安國力也。
value.en: The Han envoy reported back; the Liang crisis dissolved—through Han Anguo's doing.
value.literal: The Han envoy returned and reported; the Liang affair was all released—it was Anguo's strength.

value.zh: 景帝、太后益重安國。
value.en: Emperor Jing and the empress dowager prized him the more.
value.literal: Emperor Jing and the empress dowager valued Anguo all the more.

value.zh: 上怒恢不出擊單于輜重也，恢曰：「始約為入馬邑城，兵與單于接，而臣擊其輜重，可得利。
value.en: The emperor raged that Wang Hui had not attacked the baggage train. Wang Hui said, "The plan was for the shanyu to enter Mayi while the main army pinned him; I was to fall on his wagons.
value.literal: The emperor was angry that Hui had not gone out to strike the shanyu's baggage train; Hui said, "The original agreement was that he would enter Mayi city, troops would engage the shanyu, and your servant would strike his baggage train—gain could be had.

value.zh: 今單于不至而還，臣以三萬人眾不敵，祗取辱。
value.en: He never came; my thirty thousand could not have beaten his host—I would only have shamed the throne.
value.literal: Now the shanyu did not arrive but returned; your servant with thirty thousand men could not match the enemy—he would only fetch disgrace.

value.zh: 固知還而斬，然完陛下士三萬人。」
value.en: I knew retreat meant death, but I saved your thirty thousand men."
value.literal: Your servant knew that returning meant execution, yet he preserved Your Majesty's thirty thousand men intact."
